## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Movie Boys in Peril; or, Strenuous Days Along the Panama Canal"
Author: Victor Appleton (Garden City Publishing, 1926). Gutenberg #76378. Juvenile adventure. Chapters I–XXV, no Part headings. Last line: "...we will take leave of the moving picture boys." Ends "THE END." Series list at back: next volume "The Movie Boys Under the Sea; or The Treasure of the Lost Ship."

### Main characters
- **Joe Duncan** – moving picture boy, Joe is chum; Joe has a patent application pending for a focusing tube; loves a "great head for figures"; Birdie Lee and Mabel Pierce are the girls of the company (Joe's interest: Mabel; Blake teases re Birdie Lee).
- **Blake Stewart** – the other moving picture boy; more serious, deeper thinker; reads history; "Blake was modest."
- **Calvert Hadley** – head of Film Theatrical Company (outdoor pictures); writes letters.
- **Mr. Ringold** – Film company, dramatic side.
- **C. C. Piper ("Gloomy")** – grouchy actor; predicts "buried alive under one of the big Culebra slides."
- **Birdie Lee** (pretty, vivacious), **Mabel Pierce** (new member), **Nettie "Miss" Shay**, **Henry Robertson** (juvenile leads).
- **Vigues Alcando** (Mr. Alcando) – young Spaniard/South American, Equatorial Railroad Co. (Brazilian railroad in fact); smokes cigars; ticking "alarm clock" = brass-bound timer/bomb; villain, plotted to fake-dynamite Gatun Dam to scare shippers; disappears at end.
- **Hank Duryee** – town livery driver at Central Falls; horse **Rex** (killed in fall).
- **Mr. Hiram Baker** – farmer whose farm the boys board on near Central Falls; Mrs. Baker.
- **Sam** – red-haired, barefoot farmer's son; delivers special delivery letter from **Sim Rolinson** (postmaster)'s mistake; his father forgot letter in pocket.
- **Captain Watson** – commander of government tug **Nama** (sunk after collision with Brazilian steamer; Captain Martail of that steamer, a "distant relative" of Alcando).
- **Captain Wiltsey** – commander of tug **Bohio** (later); canal employee.
- **Ramo** – educated Indian guide in jungle; shot alligator.
- **General George W. Goethals** – chief engineer (mentioned).
- Tug/boats: **Gatun**(liner), **Nama**, **Bohio**. Motor cycle owned jointly by boys (fast, ~90 mph).
- Hotel: Washington Hotel, Colon. Hotel at Central Falls; uptown NY hotel for Alcando.
- Canal details: Culebra Cut nine miles, avg depth 120 ft, sides up to 500 ft; Gold Hill highest point; Gatun Dam 1½ miles long, 105 ft high; Gatun Lake 85 ft above sea; Toro Point breakwater 11,000 ft; Pedro Miguel 30⅓ ft lock; Miraflores 54⅔ ft in two locks; gates 65 ft wide, 7 ft thick, 600 tons; emergency dams swing into place in 2 minutes electrically, 30 min by hand; fender chain steel links 3 in thick, stops ship ~70 ft, 100-ton pressure to yield, 250+ to break.
- Other: Chagres River; Central Falls; Ritzen not in this book.

### Event sequence
1. Ch I–II: Boys at Baker farm, Central Falls, on vacation; new motor cycle. Runaway horse Rex with carriage (Hank Duryee, Alcando) heads for broken bridge over ravine (temporary road, sharp curve). Boys chase on motor cycle, cut across meadow; motor cycle breaks gasoline pipe; horse crashes through barrier, carriage catches on king beam of bridge, horse dies in ravine (100 ft deep).
2. Ch III–IV: Boys pull carriage back. Alcando (faint cut on head), says he is Spanish-speaking; gives card "Vigues Alcando." Letter from Mr. Hadley falls from his pocket addressed to Blake & Joe. Letter text: introduces Alcando, mentions Panama, a monstrous Culebra slide impending. Alcando's explanation: Equatorial Railroad Co. wants films; he came to NY, Hadley introduced him.
3. Ch V: Sam delivers delayed special delivery letter. Hadley letter (full text in ch V): big Culebra slide predicted (man who lived in Panama), warns of "Spanish gentleman named Vigues Alcando"; boys decide yes.
4. Ch VI: Blake reads "History of the Panama Canal" at library; decide go. Alcando at hotel; shuffles papers; loose sheet "...go to Panama, get all the pictures you can, especially the big guns...."
5. Ch VII: Alcando explains "guns/ones" mistake. NY: Piper's gloom. Mr. Hadley: investigated credentials; "no South American spy." Alcando's hotel room: cigar smoke of unnamed visitor; brass box on table.
6. Ch VIII–IX: Sail on steamer Gatun (via San Juan, Porto Rico). Stateroom ticking box in Alcando's berth (brass-bound box with metal projections). Alcando explains as "new alarm clock."
7. Ch X–XI: Colon; Washington Hotel; night balcony conference: "Are you sure the machine works right?" Government tug Nama leaves; runner: "You will not fail us?"; Alcando: "I will not fail—if I have to sacrifice myself."
8. Ch XII: Gatun locks: fender chain, lock gates, tug pulled backward toward closing gates by stern locomotives (signal failure), stopped in time. Water filling.
9. Ch XIII–XIV: Jungle trip up Chagres; leaf-cutting ants; tapirs; orchids (Holy Ghost); iguanas (tied legs); alligator attacks Blake in river; Ramo shoots it.
10. Ch XV–XVI: Culebra Cut; Alcando mutters "Dynamite"; cover story.
11. Ch XVII–XVIII: Brazilian steamer rams Nama against central pier; Nama sinks; boys transfer to Bohio. Miraflores: upper gate opened error; emergency dam saves Bohio; boys film it.
12. Ch XIX–XXI: Culebra big slide, Joe buried under camera, rescued by Blake & Alcando; Gatun Dam; Alcando's absence; Joe overhears "I'll not put the blame on..."
13. Ch XXII–XXIII: Alcando's letter fragment: "Stuff is all ready... get away... fine scenery in Europe." Captain Wiltsey warns: rumor Gatun Dam to be dynamited tonight; flashlight/automatic camera trap prepared.
14. Ch XXIV–XXV: Ticking sound near spillway; Blake cuts wires of the brass box; Alcando caught on camera film. Confession: sabotage plot by Brazilian railroad stockholder to scare shippers; Alcando escapes from prison that night, vanishes; stockholder and Alcando later seen in European capital (rumored). Boys take pleasure trip; Blake gets letter, "Back... To New York."
- Mr. Piper's gloomy prediction ("look out for the big slides") as running joke.

### Quoted/numbered details worth keeping
- Motor cycle top speed "ninety miles an hour."
- Mr. Hadley's letter: "Johnnie on the Spot."
- Canal: Suez "a farm ditch" alongside Culebra.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Top of the World" by Ethel M. Dell (1920), Gutenberg #12360
Dedication: "To the precious memory of my mother." Epigraph poem ("When you have reached the top of the world...").
Structure: PART I (Ch I–XII), PART II (Ch I–XI), PART III (Ch I–XII), PART IV (Ch I–XIII). Chapter titles listed in Contents.

### Characters
- **Sylvia Ingleton** – heroine, tawny/red-brown hair, red-brown eyes, age 23 at start (was 18 when meeting Guy five years earlier); only child of **Squire Gilbert Ingleton** of the Manor; mother dead 3 years (name not given in text beyond "Mrs. Ingleton" first mother). Inherits money from mother at 25.
- **Guy Ranger** – son of Squire's former bailiff (Ranger, yeoman stock); public school educated; sent to South Africa (cousin farming); Sylvia's fiancé; falls into drink, morphine (Kieff's remedy), gambling; "Guy" calls Sylvia "darling," "sweetheart," "Cherry-ripe" used by Preston.
- **Mrs. Caroline Emmott Ingleton** (step-mother; "Madam"; formerly Mrs. Emmott, a widow) – tall, handsome, domineering, jealous; plots with Preston; steals/suppresses Guy's letters.
- **Jeffcott** – old head gardener; "Miss Sylvia"; tells Sylvia Guy's letter came Friday.
- **George Preston** – "the M.F.H."/Captain Preston; little man, horsey, rich from Turf; wants Sylvia; they become "engaged provisionally."
- **Vernon Eversley** – friendly young man.
- **Bliss** – butler; **Mrs. Hadlow** – housekeeper.
- **Burke Ranger** – Guy's cousin, a rugged man, tanned, grey eyes ("eagle eyes," "steel-grey"), no fashionable looks; owns **Blue Hill Farm** near **Ritzen** (railway station) and Brennerstadt; ~20 miles away. Calls Sylvia "partner," "little pal," "Enchantress" (nickname). Ironic, stern, moral. Pipe smoker.
- **Mary Ann** – hideous, lame Kaffir housekeeper; **Joe** – Kaffir houseboy; **Fair Rosamond ("Rose")** – Kaffir girl; **Hans Schafen** – Dutch overseer (rubber-soled boots).
- **Piet Vreiboom** – Boer neighbour; low-browed, monkeyish; insults Sylvia; Kieff's ally.
- **Saul Kieff** – sinister Jewish-looking doctor ("raven," onyx eyes, "vampire"); remedy = morphia injection; struggles with Burke; Burke thrashes him at Brennerstadt; Kieff later dies of opium overdose at Hoffstein's.
- **Bill Merston** – red-faced jovial neighbour (farm 12 miles away); **Matilda Merston** – thin, bitter, pale-eyed; six infants died; becomes Sylvia's friend.
- **Donovan Kelly ("Donovan"/Kelly)** – Irish manager of a diamond mine, Brennerstadt; horse **St. Peter ("Pete")**; ex-Imperial Yeomanry; hearty friend.
- **Hoffstein** – bar owner in Brennerstadt; **Wilbraham** – diamond owner, raffle of big diamond (won by Guy).
- Horse **Diamond** – Sylvia's black horse with white head mark; wedding gift from Burke. Horse **Winnie** (Squire's horse, mentioned).
- "Piet Vreiboom" also described in "Kaffir" context.

### PART I (Ch I–XII)
- Ch I "Advice": Jeffcott in vinery urges Sylvia to marry; she is still loyal to Guy; backstory: Guy banished to South Africa 5 years ago; Squire's new wife Mrs. Emmott; Sylvia's father remarried; Sylvia's birthday/inheritance at 25.
- Ch II "The New Mistress": Mrs. Ingleton arrives; "You shall call me Madam!"; Preston appears; Preston and Mrs. Ingleton make a deal (diamonds).
- Ch III "The Whip-Hand": Mrs. Ingleton tells Gilbert she'll marry Sylvia to Preston within a year; threatens Sylvia; "whip-hand is mine."
- Ch IV "The Victor": Hunt Ball; Preston forces engagement ("provisional"); Sylvia asks to cable Guy first.
- Ch V "The Miracle": Jeffcott reveals Guy's letter arrived Friday; Sylvia confronts Mrs. Ingleton (letters stolen); announces leaving; Squire lets her go; Preston's comic dismissal; Mrs. Ingleton locked up in boudoir.
- Ch VI "The Land of Strangers": Sylvia arrives Ritzen; Guy absent; "Burke Ranger" (cousin) meets her; Guy has delirium tremens, "I'm not Guy at all." Guy's cable said come.
- Ch VII "The Wrong Turning": Burke explains Guy drinks; suggests marrying someone else. Sylvia insists on seeing Guy; Burke agrees to drive her; promise: she won't marry Guy for sacrifice.
- Ch VIII "The Comrade": Ride in cart; Ritter Spruit; picnic; "I like a man to be just a jolly comrade."
- Ch IX "The Arrival": Storm, Burke carries her in; Mary Ann; knee injury; Ritter Spruit flooded.
- Ch X "The Dream": Dream of two horsemen collision on a ledge (Guy & Burke); Burke says Guy gone (cleared out). Sylvia dreams Guy falls.
- Ch XI "The Cross-Roads": Piet Vreiboom sees Sylvia; Burke says he told Vreiboom she is his wife; proposes marriage; Sylvia accepts with conditions ("pals"). Guy's photograph in her trunk.
- Ch XII "The Stake": Brennerstadt; civil marriage; race to blasted tree (skeleton tree); Burke carves "Fide et Amore" on it; kiss, "pals" terms.

### PART II (Ch I–XI)
- Ch I "Comrades": Sylvia manages farm; Burke whips Joe with sjambok; Sylvia mends shirt; guest hut—Guy's hut ("cabin") near the spruit below kopje; Burke says he left Guy there.
- Ch II "The Visitors": Mr. and Mrs. Merston visit; Mrs. Merston's cruel prediction; "six children all dead."
- Ch III "The Bargain": Sylvia climbs kopje; Burke asks her to be his "rare shy bird"; she asks him to find Guy and save him; Burke agrees on condition "straight game"; Guy tending bar at Hoffstein's in Brennerstadt; Sylvia kisses Burke's cheek.
- Ch IV "The Capture": Burke and Kelly go to Hoffstein's; Kelly lures Guy; Burke takes Guy back to hotel room.
- Ch V "The Good Cause": Burke confronts Guy; Guy throws glass, fight, Burke bleeds on chin; Burke's self-reflection (house on rock).
- Ch VI "The Return": Burke brings Guy's attendance? Burke returns alone late at night; Sylvia prepares hut for Guy; Burke's chin cut ("shaving"); Burke kisses Sylvia passionately; Sylvia says "partner dear"; reconciliation.
- Ch VII "The Guest": Guy visits; drinks lager; cough; Burke takes Guy's gun; Sylvia tries to keep Guy.
- Ch VIII "The Interruption": Burke and Guy smoke; Sylvia cuts wool/socks talk; gunshot: Guy has shot himself in chest (wound); Burke fetches doctor.
- Ch IX "The Abyss": Sylvia watches Guy; Guy asks forgiveness "boss shot"; "God bless you."
- Ch X "The Desire to Live": Kieff (Saul Kieff) arrives with Burke; treats Guy; tells Sylvia she must give Guy will to live; Burke kisses her sleeping.
- Ch XI "The Remedy": Kieff's morphia remedy; Guy kisses Sylvia; Burke threatens "right is mine."

### PART III (Ch I–XII)
- Ch I "The New Era": Sylvia takes morphia from Kieff; Burke discovers; sends Kieff away; Sylvia's "top of the world" dream.
- Ch II "Into Battle": Guy recovered; Burke orders Sylvia to visit Merstons; challenge; Sylvia gives in ("I give you best, partner").
- Ch III "The Seed": Matilda Merston friendship begins.
- Ch IV "Mirage": Sylvia whips Rosamond; Guy says "marry because he was like you"; Guy kisses hand.
- Ch V "Everybody's Friend": Sand-storm; Burke kisses Sylvia brandingly; Kelly arrives; Burke's strong-box key left with Sylvia.
- Ch VI "The Hero": Guy and Burke come back; Guy hero of veldt fire, saved Burke from pinned shed; Guy drinks again.
- Ch VII "The Net": Guy at night at window; "Love that hath us in the net"; Guy takes money from box (key).
- Ch VIII "The Summons": Burke leaves for Merstons (Merston injured); "Are you still hating me?"
- Ch IX "For the Sake of the Old Love": Sylvia finds key in lock; finds cigarette in envelope; resolves to save Guy alone.
- Ch X "The Bearer of Evil Tidings": Kieff at farm tells Kelly Sylvia has eloped with Guy (lie); Kelly storms.
- Ch XI "The Sharp Corner": Sylvia goes to Brennerstadt by train; Hoffstein's girl; Burke enters with murderous look; Sylvia thinks he's a murderer.
- Ch XII "The Cost": Burke interrogates; she locks door, puts key in bosom; "I am yours"; "So...you have counted the cost?"

### PART IV (Ch I–XIII)
- Ch I "Sand of the Desert": Sylvia returns money? Burke demands; Sylvia asks him to forgive Guy; she tells him "I am yours"; silence begins.
- Ch II "The Skeleton Tree": Kelly rides with Sylvia; tells her Guy took key; returns money; "Fide et Amore" on tree.
- Ch III "The Punishment": Kieff insults Sylvia at hotel; Burke thrashes Kieff; forces apology.
- Ch IV "The Evil Thing": Burke says he kept his promise not to pursue Guy; Kelly sends money packet; Kieff found dead (opium).
- Ch V "The Land of Blasted Hopes": Return home; Sylvia replaces money; Burke has key; drought, "land of blasted hopes."
- Ch VI "The Parting": Sylvia goes to Merstons; Burke kisses her on the cart wheel; "Good-bye."
- Ch VII "Piet Vreiboom": Sylvia & Matilda friendship; Burke's note; Vreiboom visits; Sylvia tells Matilda about Guy.
- Ch VIII "Out of the Depths": Guy visits Sylvia at night (storm); tries to force her; Sylvia gives him remedy; Guy confesses his remorse; Guy sleeps.
- Ch IX "The Meeting": Burke rides to Merstons' farm; confronts Guy at hut; Guy: "She'll be true to you as long as you live."
- Ch X "The Truth": Burke with Matilda; she admits Sylvia loved Guy; Burke: "I am going back."
- Ch XI "The Storm": drought ruin; storm; Burke goes toward hut in flood.
- Ch XII "The Sacrifice": Burke finds Guy and Sylvia in hut (Sylvia protecting Guy); Burke spares Guy; they escape on Diamond; hut swept away; Burke and Sylvia reconcile; "Top of the world."
- Ch XIII "By Faith and Love": Guy dies; Burke forgave; Sylvia admits she loves Burke; Guy's diamond (won by Guy) sold; they plan to visit England and return. Final: "And they were nearer to the stars...than to the world."

### Key quoted phrases
- "Fide et Amore" (By Faith and Love), carved on skeleton tree.
- "Top of the world" (theme; Burke's and Sylvia's imagined castle "at the top of the world").
- "Land of strangers" (Sylvia's phrase for South Africa).
- "partner"/"pals" used by Burke and Sylvia.
- "Love that hath us in the net / Can he pass and we forget?" (Guy's song).
- "Johnnie"? (not in book 2).
